as_told.title: Steinman's book and FOIA on the Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit

plain: The claim is that the US Army once had an office called the Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit, or IPU, a unit said to have dealt with UFO matters. The public learned of it, the story goes, through the work of a researcher named William Steinman (also called Bill Steinman). A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb tells Michels that the IPU 'was kind of discovered through' FOIA requests in 1986 and 1987, by 'researchers such as William Steinman.' FOIA is a US law that lets anyone request government records. UAPGerb names the researcher Kevin Randall as part of the same effort and points to the government's replies about the IPU. Michels tells the story himself in a later episode: 'The fact that we had an organization called an interplanetary phenomenon unit, we know due to Bill Steinman and his work.' He places the unit in roughly 1947 to 1950 and links the find to Steinman's book UFO Crash at Aztec, which the tellers date to 1986. If the claim holds, the Army had a named office for UFOs long before the public knew it.
